evidence.claim: Blind held-out quality: promoted mean=85.125, random subset (seed=20260824) mean=54.000, title-length decorative bar mean=50.500. The promoted set beats both by >15 points, so the bar is not a random subset of the same size wearing a different name.

Field-completeness validation on every promoted card: 8/8 complete, 0 incomplete. Injecting a missing mechanism, cost, risk or evidence field into a clone of a promoted card makes validate_card fire in all four cases.

negative_controls.description: Clone a promoted card and strip each required field. validate_card must fire; a silent completeness check is a no-op.
A title-length promoter of the same cardinality must not beat the documented random subset by the same 15-point margin the maturity bar achieves. Long titles were planted on immature ideas.

question_answered: What fraction of raw ideas survive promotion, and is the bar doing work — would a random subset of the same size be indistinguishable from the promoted set on an independent quality rating?

residual_unknowns.claim: Held-out quality labels on the planted ledger were assigned by the same implementer who wrote the bar. The probes prove the bar does not read those labels and that a title-length bar fails the same comparison; they do not prove the bar tracks an independently elicited human quality rating on a live council transcript.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Score a held-out live ledger with a rater who has not seen promotion status, then re-run probe2 without replanting labels.
